objects: E is a finite-dimensional real inner-product normed additive group with its Borel measurable structure. V:E→R is the potential. Parameters α,β are nonnegative real numbers and η is real. Position/momentum states are z=(x,v)∈E×E. A record r lies in Rrec=(R≥0×(E×E))⊕Unit: live(a,z) records a finite accumulated time and a phase-space state, and dead is the separate right tag. The probability space Ω=R^N has product rate-one exponential law P. H_n:Ω→Rrec^{Fin(n+1)} is the full finite record history; D=d(H_n) is a nonnegative finite history-dependent duration.
domains: α,β∈R≥0; η∈R; y,xRef∈E; z0∈E×E; n∈N. The deterministic waiting-time input e∈R≥0; τ takes values R≥0∪{∞}. The flow time variable t∈R, cumulative-rate duration u∈R≥0, sequence w∈R^N, and ε(w,k)=max(w_k,0)∈R≥0. Histories h∈Rrec^{Fin(n+1)} are arbitrary tuples, including unrealizable tuples. d:Rrec^{Fin(n+1)}→R≥0 is Borel measurable; A⊆Rrec^{Fin(n+1)} is Borel measurable. Survival weights lie in [0,∞], with their claimed bound ≤1.
quantifiers: After fixing the ambient E, V, α, β, η and all listed hypotheses, all displayed c, Φ, S, rate, Λ, τ, next, record, P, ε, H, L, W are let-defined. Then for every y∈E, for every xRef∈E, for every z0∈E×E, for every n∈N, and for every function d on the entire length-(n+1) record-history space, Measurable(d) implies a four-part conjunction. The final part is quantified over every measurable history set A. No almost-everywhere restriction is attached to the first three conclusions, including the weight bound for every arbitrary history h. The probability identity holds exactly for each choice of these quantified data.
assumptions: Globally on E: V is twice continuously Fréchet differentiable. α>0 and α≤β. For every x,v∈E, α||v||² ≤ ((D(DV))(x)[v])[v] ≤ β||v||². Also η>0 and βη≤1. All indicated spaces use the Borel/product/sum measurable structures. There are no additional restrictions on y, xRef, z0, n or measurable d. In particular, d need not be bounded, positive, deterministic, or restricted to histories that the recursion attains. The full space E may have dimension zero.
conclusion:
For fixed y,xRef,z0,n and measurable d, let h_n denote the last entry h[n]. Then:
(1) {(h,w)∈Rrec^{Fin(n+1)}×R^N : L(y,xRef,h_n,d(h),w_0)} is measurable. This displayed auxiliary joint event uses coordinate 0, independently of the theorem's n.
(2) h↦W(y,xRef,h_n,d(h)) is measurable.
(3) For every history h, W(y,xRef,h_n,d(h))≤1.
(4) For every measurable A⊆Rrec^{Fin(n+1)},
P{w:H_n(w)∈A and L(y,xRef,record(y,xRef,z0,ε(w),n),d(H_n(w)),w_n)}
= ∫_A W(y,xRef,h_n,d(h)) (H_n#P)(dh).
The integral is an extended nonnegative Lebesgue integral with restriction to A, not a normalized conditional integral. The final state equals H_n(w)[n] by definition. Thus the tested law is the strict survival of the next wait at a duration chosen from the entire finite record history. The explicit test class is all measurable history events A and all measurable finite nonnegative durations d.
scopes: The fourth assertion concerns the nth fresh exponential threshold w_n conditional on records indexed 0 through n: computing record n uses thresholds 0 through n−1. It includes all previous record times and phase-space states, and the dead tag. The measurable weight and its bound hold on the whole abstract history space, not just almost surely under the history distribution. No assertion concerns arbitrary externally enlarged histories, histories depending on w_n, random durations depending on future thresholds, or infinite values of d. The auxiliary joint-measurability claim concerns arbitrary histories paired with a fresh real sequence, and is different from the probability event using w_n. If expressed through conditional expectation, the probability identity identifies the corresponding history-measurable representative almost surely; it does not assert a pointwise conditional probability for every zero-probability history.

definitions:
Use the following literal definitions, with real division total (a/0=0):
c(y,xRef)=y−η∇V(xRef).
Φ(y,xRef,t,(x,v))=(c+cos(t)(x−c)+sqrt(η)sin(t)v, −sin(t)/sqrt(η)(x−c)+cos(t)v).
Writing g=∇V(x)−∇V(xRef), S(xRef,(x,v))=(x,v−(2⟨v,g⟩/||g||²)g).
rate(xRef,(x,v))=sqrt(η)max(0,⟨v,∇V(x)−∇V(xRef)⟩).
Λ(y,xRef,z,u)=∫_0^u rate(xRef,Φ(y,xRef,s,z)) ds.
τ(y,xRef,z,e)=inf{t∈R≥0:Λ(y,xRef,z,t)−e≥0}, with inf(empty)=∞.
next(y,xRef,e,dead)=dead. For live(a,z), if τ(y,xRef,z,e)=∞, next=dead; otherwise, writing q=τ(y,xRef,z,e), next=live(a+q,S(xRef,Φ(y,xRef,q,z))). The literal Lean finite extraction is untopD(τ,0), used only after the infinity branch has been excluded.
record(y,xRef,z0,e,0)=live(0,z0); record(...,e,k+1)=next(y,xRef,e_k,record(...,e,k)).
P=⊗_{k∈N}Exp(rate=1) on R^N; ε(w,k)=max(w_k,0).
H_n(w)_j=record(y,xRef,z0,ε(w),j), for j=0,...,n.
L(y,xRef,live(a,z),u,e) means u<τ(y,xRef,z,max(e,0)), with u embedded into R≥0∪{∞}; L(y,xRef,dead,u,e) is false.
W(y,xRef,live(a,z),u)=ofReal(exp(−Λ(y,xRef,z,u))); W(y,xRef,dead,u)=0. ofReal embeds max(value,0) into extended nonnegative reals. The accumulated timestamp a is ignored by L and W; their duration is measured afresh from z.
